sections.heading: 1. Key Expressions & Sentences Reviewed (Lessons 43–49)
points: Lesson 43: "Ndinokumbirawo undibatsire basa iri, riri kundinetsa zvikuru." — Please help me with this work; it is giving me a lot of trouble.
Lesson 44: "Akadanidzira achiti, "Batai mbavha iyo!"" — He shouted, "Catch that thief!"
Lesson 45: "Unofunga kuti mvura ichanaya here mangwana?" — Do you think it will rain tomorrow?
Lesson 46: "Kwedu kune makomo marefu anonakidza kuona." — In our home region there are tall mountains that are wonderful to see.
Lesson 47: "Ugosvika pano manhero kuti tigozodya tese." — Be sure to arrive here in the evening so that we can eat together.
Lesson 48: "Mvura iri kunaya zvakanyanya kunze uko nhasi." — It is raining heavily outside there today.
Lesson 49: "Nekuda kwekushanda nesimba, akawana mubayiro." — Because of working hard, he received a reward.

sections.heading: 2. Core Shona Grammar Rules Consolidated
points: Actions Happening Right Now: The '-ri ku-' Progressive: [Subject + -ri] + ku-[verb] -> Ndiri kuverenga (I am reading) | Vari kufamba (They are walking) | Mvura iri kunaya (It is raining)
Giving Commands & Polite Requests ('Batai'): Singular Command: Verb stem (-a) [Huya! / Tora!] | Polite or Plural Command: Verb stem + -i (-ai) [Huyai! / Torai!]
Present Tense & Everyday Actions ('Unofunga'): [ndi- (I) / u- (you) / a- (he/she) / ti- (we) / va- (they)] + -no- + verb -> Ndinoda (I want), Vanogara (They live)
Present Tense & Everyday Actions ('anonakidza'): [ndi- (I) / u- (you) / a- (he/she) / ti- (we) / va- (they)] + -no- + verb -> Ndinoda (I want), Vanogara (They live)
Shona Greetings & Time of Day ('manhero'): Morning: Mangwanani | Afternoon: Masikati | Evening: Manheru | How are you?: Makadini? / Wakadii?
Talking About the Past ('zvakanyanya'): Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb

sections.heading: 3. Cultural Context & Practical Usage
points: Polite Requests for Help ('Ndinokumbirawo') with Difficult Tasks: Adding the suffix '-wo' ('please / kindly') to 'ndinokumbira' ('I ask') creates 'Ndinokumbirawo'—the most natural, polite way in Shona to ask a colleague, mentor, or family member for guidance when a task proves challenging..
Community Vigilance & Neighbourhood Solidarity in Zimbabwe: In Zimbabwean townships ('marukisheni') and villages alike, neighbours know one another well and look out for each other's homes.

Zimbabwe's Three Seasons & Reading the Signs of Rain ('Mvura'): Because rain-fed agriculture sustains millions of livelihoods, predicting whether it will rain tomorrow ('kuti mvura ichanaya here mangwana') is a national pastime from October to March.

Zimbabwe's Dramatic Mountain Landscapes ('Makomo Marefu'): From the mist-covered peaks of the Eastern Highlands—Mount Nyangani (2,592m), the Chimanimani Mountains, and the Bvumba—to the ancient granite inselbergs ('makomo') and balancing rocks of Matobo, Domboshava, and Epworth, mountain landscapes hold deep scenic and historical significance across Zimbabwe..

review_exercises.prompt: Review 7 — Home & Living Room Vocabulary: What is 'imba yokutandarira' in English?
options: The kitchen where food is prepared
The living room / sitting room (room for socializing)
The outdoor granary for storing maize
The classroom at a secondary school
review_exercises.correct_answer: The living room / sitting room (room for socializing)
review_exercises.explanation: From '-tandara' (spend time chatting/socializing), 'imba yokutandarira' is the living room.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 7 — Spatial Prepositions: How do you say 'in the middle of the room' in Shona?
options: pamusoro peimba
parutivi peimba
pakati peimba
seri kweimba
review_exercises.explanation: 'Pakati pe-' means 'in the middle / centre of'.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 7 — Kitchen Appliances: Which Shona sentence describes 'a white refrigerator and brown cupboards'?
options: tebhuro diki nezvigaro zviviri
gaba remaruva nemabhuku matatu
hwindo guru nemusuwo muchena
firiji chena nemakabati ebhurauni
review_exercises.explanation: 'Firiji chena' = 'white refrigerator', and 'nemakabati ebhurauni' = 'and brown cupboards'.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 7 — Describing Objects: In 'gaba remaruva rine ruvara rwebhuruu', what is blue?
options: The flower vase
The flowers inside the garden
The wooden table in the corner
The curtain on the window
review_exercises.explanation: 'Gaba remaruva' means 'flower vase / pot of flowers', and 'rine ruvara rwebhuruu' means 'it has a blue colour'.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 7 — Garden Tools: What are 'badza, foshoro, nehara' used for?
options: Cooking sadza and relish in the kitchen
Cultivating the field and tending the garden (hoe, shovel, and rake)
Writing examinations in a school classroom
Repairing minibuses and trucks in town
review_exercises.correct_answer: Cultivating the field and tending the garden (hoe, shovel, and rake)
review_exercises.explanation: 'Badza' is a hand hoe, 'foshoro' is a shovel/spade, and 'hara' is a garden rake.

review_exercises.prompt: Review 7 — Translate this new review sentence: 'Pamusoro petebhuro pane gaba remaruva machena.'
options: Beside the house there is a large green water tank.
Inside the kitchen there are four chairs and a stove.
On top of the table there is a vase of white flowers.
Underneath the tree there are farm tools and buckets.
review_exercises.correct_answer: On top of the table there is a vase of white flowers.
review_exercises.explanation: 'Pamusoro petebhuro' = 'On top of the table', 'pane' = 'there is', 'gaba remaruva machena' = 'a vase of white flowers'.
